source.title_on_document: Human Creativity in the Age of LLMs: Randomized Experiments on Divergent and Convergent Thinking

supplement.where: Appendices A and B are inside this PDF (pp. 16-18). The two preregistrations are at https://aspredicted.org/dkvp-n785.pdf (Experiment 1, p. 4 footnote 1) and https://aspredicted.org/4q75-bskd.pdf (Experiment 2, p. 9 footnote 2).
supplement.holds: Appendices hold only the GPT-4o settings, the system prompts (Figures 11 and 12), and sample LLM responses (Tables 1 and 2). No supplementary statistics are referenced. Arm sizes, arm means, SDs, and standard errors are not printed anywhere in this PDF; most results are Kruskal-Wallis/Dunn p-values and figures with SE error bars.

paper_design_summary: Two preregistered online experiments on Prolific (US/UK). In each, participants were randomly assigned to no AI, a standard GPT-4o arm that gives ideas or answers, or a coach-like GPT-4o arm that gives strategies or associated words, for three exposure rounds; after a one-minute Snake distractor game all participants did the task again without AI. Experiment 1 (n = 460 recruited) used the Alternate Uses Test, scored for originality (fine-tuned GPT-3 scorer), fluency, and SBERT idea diversity at the individual and group level; Experiment 2 (n = 640 recruited) used the Remote Associates Test, scored for accuracy.

assignment.what_was_assigned: Type of GPT-4o response shown during three exposure rounds of the AUT: none, a List of Ideas (7 sampled GPT-4o alternate uses), or a List of Strategies (7 SCAMPER-based prompts, no answers). The test round was unassisted for everyone.
assignment.quote: During the exposure phase, participants are introduced to three objects, one after the other. Every participant was randomly assigned to receive one of three types of LLM responses
assignment.prereg_locator: p. 4, footnote 1 (https://aspredicted.org/dkvp-n785.pdf); p. 6, Section 3.1.4 "Following our pre-registration"

arms.name: None (No LLM Response)
arms.description: Control group. No LLM support provided.

arms.name: List of Ideas (LLM Ideas)
arms.description: GPT-4o generated alternate uses for the object; seven randomly sampled uses were shown and participants could freely use them.

arms.name: List of Strategies (LLM Strategies)
arms.description: GPT-4o with a SCAMPER system prompt (Figure 11) generated seven strategies; it guided participants but did not share explicit answers.

participants.exclusions: Not stated. The paper gives 460 recruited (Figure 2 shows n = 460 entering randomization, 33.3% per condition) and 9,457 ideas analyzed; it gives no per-arm counts and no count of participants analyzed.
participants.who: Prolific participants based in the US or UK and fluent in English; paid $1.57 for about 12 minutes
participants.locator: p. 6, Section 3.1.5; p. 4, Figure 2 (n = 460); p. 6, Section 3.2 (9,457 ideas)

ai_tool.how_used: Static output, not a chat. Five seconds after each object appeared, the assigned GPT-4o response appeared character by character beside the idea entry box. List of Ideas = 7 GPT-4o uses (ideas_supplied); List of Strategies = 7 SCAMPER prompts with no examples (coach). Settings in Appendix A.1, p. 16.

task.description: Alternate Uses Test: list creative uses for an everyday object (items sampled from tire, pants, shoe, table, bottle). Three exposure rounds with the assigned AI response, a one-minute Snake distractor game, then one test round on a new object with no AI for anyone.
task.duration: Two minutes per object; about 12 minutes for the whole experiment

outcomes.name: Originality, test round (unassisted)
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Originality of each AUT idea on a 1-5 scale from a fine-tuned GPT-3 classifier (Organisciak et al. 2023), r = 0.81 with human judgments overall and r > 0.88 for the five chosen objects. Kruskal-Wallis H test across the three conditions, Dunn's test with Bonferroni correction. The paper does not say whether the test runs on ideas or on participant means; Figure 4a plots average originality of ideas.
outcomes.delay: After a one-minute Snake distractor game in the same session

contrasts.reported: Kruskal-Wallis H(2) = 9.14, p = 0.010; Dunn (Bonferroni) List of Strategies vs No LLM p = 0.009 (Strategies significantly worse)

outcomes.name: Creative flexibility (dissimilarity of test-round ideas to the participant's own exposure-round ideas)
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: For each test-round idea, the maximum cosine similarity between its embedding and all of the participant's exposure-round ideas; plotted so that a higher value means more dissimilarity (Figure 4c, "participant creative flexibility"). This is the paper's label; it compares a person's test ideas to that same person's earlier ideas, so it does not match the codebook's flexibility (category count). Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn post-hoc.
outcomes.delay: After a one-minute Snake distractor game in the same session

contrasts.reported: Kruskal-Wallis H(2) = 6.31, p = 0.043; pairwise Dunn (Bonferroni) not significant; List of Strategies vs No LLM Response p = 0.052 (test ideas more similar to exposure ideas)

outcomes.name: Group-level diversity of ideas, test round (unassisted)
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Ideas sampled across participants within condition, item, and phase; median pairwise SBERT cosine distance among 7 sampled ideas, over 150 Monte Carlo runs. Higher = more diverse, so no sign reversal is needed.
outcomes.delay: After a one-minute Snake distractor game in the same session

contrasts.reported: No test statistic printed for the test phase. Text: participants exposed to LLM-generated strategies "continued to generate more similar ideas in the test phase, even without LLM assistance". Figure 5b, error bars +/- one SE of mean.
No test statistic printed. Figure 5b shows List of Ideas below None in the test phase; Section 5.1.3 says the List of Ideas condition "did not lead to the same lasting homogenization".

diversity_detail.metric: Median pairwise cosine distance between SBERT embeddings of sampled ideas
diversity_detail.embedding_model: SBERT (Reimers and Gurevych 2019); specific checkpoint not stated
diversity_detail.computed_over: All pairs among 7 ideas randomly sampled across participants in the same condition, item, and phase; 150 Monte Carlo runs. The paper says "This sampling process reflects the number of participants in each condition" without further detail.
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Error bars are +/- one standard error of the mean (Figure 5b), apparently across Monte Carlo runs; the paper says the Kruskal-Wallis/Dunn procedure was applied to group-level diversity but prints no statistic for the test phase.
diversity_detail.notes: Sampling across Monte Carlo runs means the SE reflects resampling, not the number of participants.

assignment.what_was_assigned: Type of GPT-4o response during three exposure RAT problems: none, LLM Answer (the GPT-4o solution), or LLM Guidance (five associated words per cue word, no solution). Two test rounds were unassisted for everyone.
assignment.quote: During the exposure phase, participants were required to solve three RAT problems consecutively. They were randomly assigned to one of three conditions, each providing different types of LLM assistance
assignment.prereg_locator: p. 9, footnote 2 (https://aspredicted.org/4q75-bskd.pdf); p. 11, Section 4.1.4 "Following our pre-registration"

arms.name: None (No LLM Response / No LLM Assistance)
LLM Answer
arms.description: The answer generated by GPT-4o for the given set of words.

arms.name: LLM Guidance
arms.description: GPT-4o with a coach system prompt (Figure 12) listing five associated words for each cue word and nudging the participant, without giving the solution.

participants.exclusions: Not stated. 640 recruited (Figure 7 shows n = 640 entering randomization), "of whom 99% passed the attention check"; the paper does not say whether attention-check failures were dropped and gives no analyzed count or per-arm counts. The ANCOVA denominator df is 1256.
participants.who: Prolific participants based in the US or UK and fluent in English; paid $1.30 for about 10 minutes
participants.quote: We recruited 640 participants from Prolific (of whom 99% passed the attention check).

ai_tool.how_used: Static output shown 5 seconds after each problem, character by character; participants told they could freely use it. LLM Answer gives the solution (ideas_supplied); LLM Guidance gives associated words and encouragement but no solution (coach). Settings in Appendix B.1, p. 16.

task.description: Remote Associates Test (Bowden and Jung-Beeman items, easy and medium): find a fourth word that forms compounds with three cue words. Three exposure problems with the assigned AI response, one-minute Snake distractor, then two unassisted test problems.
task.duration: One minute per problem; about 10 minutes overall

outcomes.name: RAT accuracy, test rounds (unassisted)
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Accuracy against the single correct RAT answer (answer key, no raters; no code in the vocabulary fits exactly). ANCOVA of test-round accuracy across conditions with verbal-fluency word count as covariate, Tukey HSD post-hoc. The paper does not state the unit; the denominator df of 1256 exceeds the 640 people, which suggests one row per test response (two per participant).
outcomes.delay: After a one-minute Snake distractor game in the same session

Tukey LLM Answer vs No LLM Assistance p = 0.682
Tukey LLM Guidance vs LLM Answer p = 0.064 (described as a trend)

outcomes.question: with_ai

company_involvement.description: None stated. Authors are at the University of Toronto; GPT-4o used through its API; AUT scoring API provided by Peter Organisciak's academic group (Acknowledgments, p. 14).

eligibility.reason: Both experiments randomly assign individuals to GPT-4o assistance or no AI on a creativity task (p. 4 Section 3.1.1; p. 9 Section 4.1.1). Experiment 1 recruited 460 and Experiment 2 recruited 640 Prolific participants (pp. 6, 11); analyzed counts are not printed, but they are far above 50. Outcomes are scored on the output: AUT originality (fine-tuned GPT-3 scorer), fluency, SBERT diversity, and RAT accuracy. The paper's primary outcomes are after_ai (unassisted test round); exposure-round outcomes give with_ai; group-level diversity gives across_people (exposure) and after_ai (test). Experiment 1 is the stronger fit; Experiment 2's RAT outcome is convergent, which the codebook lists as an open question for Review 1.

one_line_finding: After AI was removed, AUT originality was lower for the List of Strategies arm than for no AI (Kruskal-Wallis H(2) = 9.14, p = 0.010; Dunn p = 0.009) and not different for List of Ideas (p = 1.000) (p. 7), and RAT test accuracy was lower for LLM Guidance than no AI by 10.6 points [95% CI -18.6, -2.7] (p. 11), while LLM Answer did not differ (p = 0.682).
open_questions: Neither experiment prints the number of participants analyzed or per-arm counts; Experiment 2 does not say whether the 1% who failed the attention check were dropped.

Experiment 1's Kruskal-Wallis tests may treat ideas, not participants, as the unit (9,457 ideas analyzed); the paper does not say. Experiment 2's ANCOVA df (2, 1256) suggests one row per test response with two responses per person and no clustering by participant.
No arm means, SDs, or standard errors are printed for Experiment 1; values exist only in Figures 4 and 5 (error bars +/- one SE). Extraction will need digitizing or the authors' data.
Group-level diversity for the test phase has no printed test statistic; its uncertainty comes from 150 Monte Carlo resamples, not from participants.

Choice of primary contrast: the codebook rule picks the arm closest to free chatbot use (List of Ideas / LLM Answer), whereas the paper's headline significant effects are for the coach arms (List of Strategies / LLM Guidance).
notes: Version on file is arXiv v2 (15 Feb 2025) in CHI '25 camera-ready format; the CHI '25 version of record is DOI 10.1145/3706598.3714198. AI was not open chat: participants saw a fixed GPT-4o response. Coach arms (List of Strategies, LLM Guidance) are ai_vs_bau against no AI; Strategies vs Ideas and Guidance vs Answer are coded ai_design with the coach arm as treatment. Individual-level idea diversity is coded flexibility (within-person variety); only the group-level Monte Carlo measure is coded diversity. The paper's 'creative flexibility' is coded other. Self-reported creativity change, AI attitudes, perceived difficulty, and perceived helpfulness (Figures 6 and 10) are self-reports and not listed as outcomes. The markdown places Section 3 heading after 3.1.1 and drops the 'Figure ??' reference; the PDF was used for all numbers.
